title: Layout continuity: progressive collapse and micro-interaction polish for cost dashboards and rollout modals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Ensure layout continuity across viewport sizes and browsers for the Console cost dashboard, rollout modal flows, and dense table surfaces. Deliver a small set of responsive rules and micro-interaction polish that prevents jarring reflow, maintains column readability at narrow widths, and keeps chart legends and controls accessible in legacy browsers. Output includes a Figma prototype, QA test matrix, and a rollout checklist for the frontend team.
acceptance_criteria: Cost dashboard tiles do not overlap or truncate at 320–1440px without horizontal scrolling
Table density control works across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge with consistent vertical rhythm
Rollout modal stacks actions consistently when keyboard navigation and screen readers are used
Charts preserve interactive tooltip placement and avoid marker clipping at smaller widths
Prototype handed off with tokens and responsive constraints; engineering sign-off on CSS approach
comments: 2025-02-11: Initial exploration — tested three collapse strategies: column collapse, card stacking, and horizontal compression. Card stacking feels most predictable for users scanning cost cards. — Aisha

2025-02-13: Engineering review: Marco recommends limiting JS-driven layout shifts and prefers CSS container queries + utilities for the first pass. Flagged potential Safari flex-gap bug on older WebKit. — Marco

2025-02-15: PM feedback: prioritize cost list and export CTA visibility; rollout modal must keep primary action above the fold for screens >=360px. Consider adding compact table mode toggle. — Priya Singh (PM)
2025-02-16: Accessibility pass: ensured focus trap in modals remains intact when content collapses; added aria-expanded states for collapsible rows. Need a11y QA on VoiceOver. — Jonas (Accessibility)
2025-02-18: Design review submitted. Prototype link and QA matrix attached. Awaiting engineering estimate for implementation and a small follow-up for legacy Edge fixes. — Aisha
notes_for_engineering: Favor CSS container queries and CSS grid/flexbox over JS layout calculations where possible
Provide a fallback layout for legacy WebKit/Edge that avoids reliance on gap in flex containers
Implement a dense-row mode with tokenized spacing so charts and tables align vertically
Add automated visual regression snapshots for 320px, 420px, 768px, 1024px, and 1440px breakpoints
